transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-03-11
Time: 14:00 - 14:52 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Location: Zoom (recording)
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Malhotra (Redwood SE), Marcus Li (NovaEdge Head of ML), Sofia Ramos (Platform), Devon Park (SRE)

Summary:
Quick POC scoping to align on workload characterization and traffic model for a 4-week POC. Focus on QPS, concurrency, token distributions, benchmark plan (steady-state & soak), and success criteria for performance/cost. Agreed: Redwood to share template and run initial hosted bench; NovaEdge to share logs + enable on-prem test.

Topics:
- QPS and concurrency targets
- Input/output token histograms and prompt variability
- Benchmark definitions: steady-state, peak soak, tail-latency checks
- Success criteria and rollback/fallback policy needs
- Timeline: 2-week prep, 2-week runs (4-week total)

Transcript:
[00:00] Avery: okay uh hey everyone thanks for joining on time, we'll run about 45-ish, 50, 52 minutes. quick intros?
[00:12] Marcus: yeah Marcus Li, head of ML at NovaEdge. We're trying to move inference off our fragile k8s stuff into a managed runtime or dedicated cluster, uh budget constraints too.
[00:18] Sofia: Sofia, platform eng, i'll be the person dealing with network and infra config.
[00:23] Devon: Devon, SRE, largely on perf and monitoring.
[00:26] Priya: Priya Malhotra, SE at Redwood - i'll walk through the traffic model and bench plan.
[00:31] Avery: top-level goal, right, is to validate throughput & p95 latency at our target QPS, and also get unit economics so you can budget. Marcus, you mentioned peaks and spiky traffic?
[00:42] Marcus: yeah in summary: average QPS around 8 to 12 during business hours, but bursts up to 40 QPS for short windows; concurrency tends to be around 15-25 depending on batching. Most requests are single-turn completions, about 60% contextual prompts where there's a 1k token context, uh not always 1k, median input tokens more like 150, mean maybe 220 because of some long tails. Output tokens average 50-80 depending on task.
[01:10] Priya: okay that helps. So to confirm: average QPS 10, burst 40, concurrency target 20. For the POC we should define explicit qps windows: baseline 10 QPS steady-state, burst flood 40 QPS for 5 minutes, and ramp tests. Does that reflect reality?
[01:25] Marcus: yes exactly, plus weekend traffic is lower but we only need to focus on business hours for SLAs.
[01:31] Devon: one additional piece, a nontrivial percent of requests come with long contexts - we estimate 8% above 1k tokens and those really hit memory / KV cache. We need to see cache hit-rate sensitivity.
[01:44] Avery: good note. Priya, can you outline what we'll need from NovaEdge to model this?
[01:50] Priya: sure, simplest: an anonymized sample of 2k requests with input token counts and output tokens, plus a time-series of QPS across a typical day (minute granularity). Also metadata on streaming vs full-blob responses. If you can include latency/cpu/gpu host metrics that's great but optional.
[02:10] Marcus: we can do that, we'll redact user ids. expect something 48 hours.
[02:15] Sofia: firewall and VPC notes - if we do on-prem runs we'll need to open ports for the runner, exceptions for the Redwood collector, that may take a week for our security to approve.
[02:26] Avery: noted, we'll mark that as a blocker for on-prem. The hosted quick-run can be done without those rules.
[02:32] Priya: going into the traffic model, some small mismatches may occur because your input token distribution is heavy-tailed. we'll compute median, 75th, 95th and max token sizes and create synthetic load that reflects those buckets. For batching heuristics we usually simulate two modes: cost-optimized (bigger batches, slightly higher latency) and latency-optimized (small batches, lower tail latencies).
[02:57] Marcus: can you share typical numbers you see for batch sizes vs latency tradeoffs?
[03:02] Priya: sure, as a rough example on a T4-class dedicated runner for a 7b-ish model: single-request real-time median latency 80-120ms per token; with batching to 8-12 concurrent requests latency grows but amortized cost per token drops ~30%. p95 depends heavily on KV cache and caching prefixes - if we get high prefix re-use the p95 can be close to median. If no cache, p95 can be 2-3x median.
[03:31] Devon: i'm hearing numbers but can you put absolute end-to-end numbers? we need p95 < 500ms for our critical flows.
[03:38] Priya: yes so baseline success criteria proposal: p50 < 200ms, p95 < 500ms at steady 10 QPS with your token distribution; during peak 40 QPS p95 < 800ms or graceful degradation to a compatible smaller model. That's a starting point for the POC.
[03:55] Marcus: that sounds reasonable, though cost is a big factor - do you have cost estimates for hosted vs dedicated for our throughput?
[04:02] Avery: we'll produce cost scenarios. rough back-of-envelope: hosted per-token ops will be higher but lower ops overhead; dedicated reserved GPU with good batching can reduce per-1k token cost by 30-50% at steady load. we'll send three scenarios: small POC hosted, dedicated reserved, and hybrid routing.
[04:20] Marcus: good. timeline?
[04:22] Priya: recommend 2-week prep to collect logs and set up configs, then 2-week run where we do incremental benching: week 1 hosted synthetic runs and baseline tuning, week 2 on-prem or dedicated soak tests. total 4 weeks.
[04:36] Sofia: security approval may push on-prem into week 3 or 4, so plan for hosted baseline first.
[04:42] Avery: agreed. Next, benchmark plan specifics: we'll do a steady-state test for 1 hour at 10 QPS, a peak soak of 5-15 minutes at 40 QPS, and a long soak 3-4 hours at 5-8 QPS to measure cost and memory growth. We'll capture p50, p95, p99 latencies, token throughput, GPU utilization, and memory/KV cache hit-rate.
[05:05] Marcus: how do you simulate the long context behavior and KV cache?
[05:09] Priya: we replay actual prefixes from your logs as synthetic sequences to recreate cache hits. for KV cache sensitivity we'll run variants: cold-start (no cache), warm cache (~50% hit), and hot cache (~80% hit). that shows sensitivity to your real workload.
[05:25] Devon: monitoring ops - we'll need tracing hooks, op-level metrics, and logs forwarded to our SIEM. Can you expose tracing tags?
[05:33] Priya: yes we support op-level traces and per-token cost breakdowns. we'll provide a tracing hook and a minimal dashboard.
[05:39] Marcus: one concern: model fallbacks during capacity spikes. can Redwood route to a cheaper model automatically? what's the behavior?
[05:47] Avery: yes routing policy can fall back to smaller model or different region; we can configure automatic fallback with a policy and circuit-breaker thresholds. important for graceful degradation.
[05:58] Marcus: perfect. also want to validate that embeddings calls (we also use embeddings for another pipeline) can be co-located or isolated.
[06:06] Priya: we recommend isolating embedding workloads in a separate route because they have different IO patterns; we can test both options during POC.
[06:12] Sofia: about data residency and logs, we need SOC2 and log retention details.
[06:16] Avery: we'll attach security pack; Redwood is SOC2-ready and can provide logs metadata and KMS integrations.
[06:22] Marcus: great. now a couple more specifics we want in the traffic model: concurrency distribution (e.g., percent of requests with concurrency > 1), throttling policy effects, and ratio of streaming responses. for our app about 30% of completions are streaming.
[06:38] Priya: noted - we'll include streaming-mode tests where we measure partial-delivery latency. that impacts tail latencies.
[06:45] Marcus: what about cold-starts and model load times? we spin down idle nodes - will that affect our p95?
[06:51] Priya: if you have aggressive scale-to-zero, yes. for POC we suggest warm pools or min replicas to avoid cold start penalties. we'll simulate with both min-replica=0 and min-replica>0 configs.
[07:05] Devon: logging of per-request token counts is important - i'll make sure logs have token_in and token_out fields.
[07:10] Marcus: ok on logs, we'll redact and deliver.
[07:12] Priya: for the synthetic load generator, we'll seed it with the token distribution buckets: 60% small (<200 tokens), 25% medium (200-800), 8% large (800-2k), 7% very large (>2k). does that align?
[07:29] Marcus: yes that's close to our internal numbers. maybe adjust small to 55% but ok.
[07:33] Priya: fine, we'll parameterize it. We'll also create a QPS schedule: baseline 10 QPS for 1 hour, then spike ramp to 40 QPS for 5 minutes, back to 10 QPS, then a sustained 4-hr soak at 5-8 QPS.
[07:48] Avery: success criteria recap: 1) functional correctness (no increased error rate vs baseline), 2) p95 latency targets (steady p95 <500ms, peak p95 <800ms), 3) throughput >= 10 QPS steady, 4) acceptable per-1k-token cost - Redwood will propose threshold numbers, 5) predictable scaling and no memory leaks during 4hr soak.
[08:12] Marcus: agreed, one addition: any model regression on quality must be flagged - we'll provide eval prompts to check generation quality and semantic fidelity.
[08:20] Priya: yes include quality checks, we'll run evals pre/post to detect regressions; if quality drops beyond a predefined threshold we treat that as failed POC.
[08:28] Devon: security: we can't send PII, so logs must be sanitized.
[08:32] Marcus: already noted we'll sanitize.
[08:34] Avery: ok timeline and owner recap.
[08:36] Avery: Priya to share template and benchmark plan by Friday (2025-03-14). Marcus to share logs by Thursday (2025-03-13). Devon to work on runner access for on-prem test by 2025-03-20. Redwood to send hosted vs dedicated cost scenarios by Friday.
[08:55] Marcus: any notes on metrics we'll expect in the report?
[08:58] Priya: p50/p95/p99 latencies, throughput, tokens/sec, GPU util, KV cache hit-rate, error rate, and cost per 1k tokens. We'll also include a summary chart of simulated QPS vs latency.
[09:14] Sofia: ok. small question - how do you simulate multi-tenant interference? we run other jobs on same infra sometimes.
[09:21] Priya: good point. we can run contention tests by introducing dusty background CPU/GPU workloads to measure isolation and performance degradation. we'll include a couple of runs like that.
[09:34] Marcus: that would be helpful.
[09:36] Avery: anything else?
[09:38] Devon: just to confirm p95 budget is negotiable, but let's start with the numbers.
[09:42] Marcus: yeah let's start.
[09:43] Priya: cool i'll follow up post-meeting with an email and attachments.
[09:47] Avery: wrap-up: we'll send the templates and schedule the run; next sync after initial data ingestion and hosted baseline - propose 2025-03-18 for a 30-min check-in.
[09:57] Marcus: 3/18 works for us.
[10:00] Meeting ends (recording stopped).

Notes about transcript quality: occasional mis-transcriptions of acronyms (KV vs K V), some speaker labels merged (Speaker 3 used briefly), filler words preserved.
